headline: Southborough officials prepared for a potential FY28 tax override as departments outlined severe cuts, while boards advanced major housing and development proposals.
synopsis: The Select Board opened preliminary FY28 budget reviews, where school, police, and fire officials warned that level funding without a tax override would trigger significant layoffs and service reductions. Concurrently, the Capital Improvement and Planning Committee grappled with a $1 million gap between town capital requests and available non-debt funding. In development matters, the Select Board voted to sponsor a Town Meeting warrant article removing the town cap on 55-plus housing developments. Meanwhile, the Planning Board reviewed lighting, landscaping, and stormwater plans for the proposed Costco project and approved removing hazardous public shade trees.

highlights.title: FY28 budget scenarios and potential override impacts
highlights.why: Town departments presented level-service and level-funded budget scenarios for FY28, warning that level funding would eliminate police positions, reduce fire staffing, and require cutting roughly 15 school staff members.

highlights.title: Senior housing cap removal proposal
highlights.why: The Select Board voted to refer to the Planning Board and sponsor an article for Town Meeting that removes Southborough's 7 percent cap on over-55 housing developments.

highlights.title: Costco site plan and environmental review
highlights.why: The Planning Board reviewed exterior lighting, native landscaping, and stormwater systems for the proposed 167,000-square-foot Costco at 21 Coslin Drive before continuing the hearing to December 14.

highlights.title: FY28 capital budget funding gap
highlights.why: Town and school capital requests reached $2.2 million, outpacing the town's $1.2 million non-debt placeholder and prompting committee discussions about adjusting borrowing thresholds.

highlights.title: Fire Department staffing and revenue risks
highlights.why: Fire officials reported that level funding would reduce shift minimums and halt regular operation of the second ambulance, which generated up to $200,000 in revenue last year.

highlights.title: Scenic road hazardous tree removals approved
highlights.why: The Planning Board and tree warden approved removing dead and hazardous trees along scenic roads, agreeing to fully remove a rotting locust tree on Pine Hill Road following abutter input.

looking_ahead.what: Continued public hearings on Costco, 0 Southville Road MBTA development, and ZBA zoning amendments
